title: Panel membership visible in the scenario trace (#3 prefactor)
description:
Make the Panel's membership visible in the scenario trace, so the Conformance Suite can see a
Reviewer that was never spawned. Pure prefactor for #3: no requirement changes, the suite stays
green, and the enumeration does not grow.

## Why

`observed_trace()` in `conformance/run` (lines 46–68) reconstructs `panel<r>:<class>` by counting
only the Reviewers that recorded a run, so three-spawned-three-ok renders as `panel<r>:all`,
byte-identical to four. The formal side has the same hole: `tools/formal/Rloop/Loop.lean:95`
makes the Panel a single `Spawn` constructor carrying a `Panel` class, and `Scenarios.lean:74`
renders it `s!"panel{r}:{panelName p}"` — there is nowhere to record *which* Reviewers ran.

**All 206 committed scenarios would stay green over an Implementation that silently ran three
Reviewers.** Same class as the CodeRabbit finding on #2.

This contradicts #3's settled comment, which said the Lean model needs no change. That is true of
the decision function and wrong about the trace, where the Suite's coverage actually lives — see
the correction comment on #3 (2026-09-20T21:28:04Z). `tools/formal/` is in scope.

## What to change

- `Spawn.panel` carries the membership.
- The render in `Scenarios.lean` emits it.
- `python3 tools/check_scenarios.py --write` rewrites all 206 rows with the longer trace token;
  commit what it writes (`AGENTS.md`: the scenarios file is rendered, not hand-kept).
- `observed_trace()` in `conformance/run` is taught to match.

## Why it does not grow the enumeration

Under today's requirements every Panel is the same four Reviewers, so membership is a constant.
The alphabet is unchanged; only the token is longer. Availability as an *axis* is a different
job and belongs with the requirement change — see the availability-scenario-axis ticket.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `conformance/scenarios.tsv` still has 206 rows, each with membership in the trace column.
- A fake scripted to skip one Reviewer **fails** a scenario that expects four. It does not today;
  that failure is the whole point of this ticket and must be demonstrated, not asserted.
- No requirement text changes. `git diff` touches only `tools/formal/`, `tools/`-written files
  and `conformance/`.

## Lands next to

`F4` ("The scenario alphabet is a choice"), whose closing line now has a sibling case: an
Implementation that passes the suite while running a three-Reviewer Panel.
close_reason: Accepted after Round 2: Panel membership is rendered and observed, timed-out Reviewers remain members, 206 scenarios preserved, omission controls S2/S38 reject skipped sol, all six gates and executable conformance with self-check pass.

title: Specify the model-availability probe and the fail-open rule (#3)
description:
Specify the model-availability probe: its command lines, when it runs, and the fail-open rule.
The first half of #3. Nothing changes about what rloop does with the answer — that is the
record-omitted-reviewer ticket.

## Why

An exhausted model does not fail fast. It hangs, writes zero bytes on both streams, and is killed
at its seat's timeout. A Reviewer seat pays `--reviewer-timeout` (1800s default) **every Round**
for a model that was never going to answer.

Verified 2026-09-20: `claude -p "/usage"` exits 0 in seconds and reports per-family limits with
reset times, and answers just as fast *through* the exhausted model, so one call covers every
claude family. codex exposes no quota at all; both codex seats share one ChatGPT account, so a
tiny `codex exec` call is the only direct probe and one probe covers both.

## Settled already (#3, do not re-derive)

- **The check runs immediately before the Panel, never at Run start.** `astra` and `sol` produced
  the same counterexample independently: an Implementer call may run for hours past a quota reset,
  so evidence gathered at Run start can suppress a Reviewer that would have answered.
- **Fail open.** Unknown availability, a probe that fails, output that does not parse, or an
  unrecognised model name MUST spawn the Reviewer normally. Only positively recognised, unexpired
  exhaustion may short-circuit.
- **Remove only, never substitute.** Substitution silently changes which model judged the work.
- **The parser lives in this Specification.** The "language-neutral" objection is answered in #3
  point 7: this set is language-neutral about the *Implementation* (`ADR-0001`) and is
  deliberately harness-specific everywhere else — it already hardcodes the model names, the
  `--effort` values and the deny list byte for byte, and `AGT-17` pins the CLI versions.

## What to change

- A new requirement for the probe's command lines, stated verbatim like every other
  (`ADR-0001`, `OVR-2`), with `tools/check_fixtures.py --write` regenerating the fixtures. Never
  edit `conformance/fixtures/` by hand.
- **Narrow `OVR-1`**, which forbids the probe as written: *"It MUST NOT parse a Reviewer's
  output, an Implementer's output, or any part of the Finished File beyond its first line."* A
  quota probe is rloop parsing a model CLI's output and acting on it. Follow `F9`'s six-day-old
  precedent exactly: it narrowed `DIR-4`'s "entire and *unparsed*" to "entire and *unmodified*"
  to admit one datum. This is the second instance of that pattern.
- `AGT-17`: record the CLI versions the `/usage` format was verified against. `AGT-17` already
  concedes this risk class — *"a flag that a newer CLI rejects is found only by a live Run"* — so
  a drifted format is not a new kind of exposure, and fail-open degrades it to doing nothing.
- `CNF` items in `06-conformance.md` for the three fail-open paths: probe fails, probe output
  does not parse, unrecognised model name. Distinguish exhaustion from a typo: verified,
  `claude -p "say hi" --model claude-bogus-9` exits 1 in seconds with
  `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]`, while exhaustion hangs with zero bytes.

## ADR

**`ADR-0006`**, not `ADR-0005`. #3's settled comment reserved 0005, and 0005 was taken on
2026-09-21 by "The operator's view has one home and Implementations point at it". Check
`docs/adr/` for the next free number before writing, not this ticket.

Subject: rloop reads a vendor's human-facing quota report and fails open. Hard to reverse,
surprising without context, and argued against by all three advisers — record what they said and
why it was overridden.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `grep` finds the probe's command line in exactly one document, and its fixture is generated.
- Every new requirement is cited by a `CNF` item. The coverage gate holds at zero with no ratchet
  baseline, so an excuse-table entry is not available here — and would be false, since #3's
  Testability section says all of this is black-box testable.
close_reason: AGT-18, RUN-21, ADR-0006; OVR-1 narrowed per F9, OVR-2/RUN-7/AGT-1/AGT-13 amended, DIR-4 rows, CNF-24-26 with implementations and a probe role in the fake. Six gates exit 0. Suite is 20/4 against rloop-bash: CNF-9/24/25/26 red until it implements the probe, which is ADR-0001's designed path.

title: Record an unavailable Reviewer in place, never drop it (#3)
description:
An unavailable Reviewer stays in the Panel and is recorded as not having run, rather than being
dropped so the Panel runs with three. The second half of #3, and the part that changes behaviour.

Depends on the availability-probe ticket: fail-open means unknown availability MUST spawn
normally, so without a probe command line this arm is unreachable in a live Run and unscriptable
in the Suite — there is nothing for a fake to answer.

## Settled already (#3, do not re-derive)

- **Record, do not drop.** Consequence: there is no Panel floor to choose. `RUN-15` already fixes
  one — one survivor is enough, zero is exit 2 — and no version of this change alters it.
  Question 1 of #3 is withdrawn.
- **"Did not run" counts toward `RUN-15`'s zero-survivor abort.** An account wholly out of quota
  therefore loses the Round: the Implementer may have run for hours and committed work, and rloop
  exits 2 with no judge and no Finished File. Accepted unchanged — four timeouts reach the
  identical exit today, two hours later, and `F10` already rejected having rloop author a
  `finished.md` of its own for precisely this case.
- **A distinct literal is required.** `REVIEWER FAILED (exit <status>)` cannot describe a call
  that never happened — there is no status — and `PRM-2` tells the Manager that line means
  `crashed or timed out`. Reusing it makes both passages false and costs the Manager the
  distinction `RUN-15`'s own rationale rests on: *"One Reviewer down is a degraded Panel the
  Manager can weigh; four down is a broken environment."*
- **No new noun.** A `Seat`/occupant split was proposed and withdrawn by its own proposer.

## What to change

- `RUN-15`: a third arm for the omitted call, and which failures count toward the abort.
- `RUN-7` §3 — *"all four Reviewer calls … started concurrently and all waited for"* — goes
  false. Amend it.
- `RUN-8`.
- `PRM-2`: the distinct literal. Amended either way, per the settled comment.
- `DIR-4`: the Feedback File's authorship when rloop writes it in the Reviewer's place, and an
  absent or empty `.err`.
- `CONTEXT.md`: the two glossary entries drafted in #3 land **here**, not earlier — the Feedback
  File entry cites a `RUN-15` clause that does not exist until this ticket.

  ```
  **Panel**:
  The **Reviewers** `AGT-11` designates for one **Round**, each a different model, run side by
  side.

  **Feedback File**:
  One **Reviewer**'s findings for one **Round**, written for the **Manager**; rloop writes it in
  the Reviewer's place when the call failed or was never made (`RUN-15`).
  _Avoid_: Review, findings file
  ```

- `PRM-4` does **not** change. `PRM-6` forbids conditional text, and "one of four independent
  Reviewers" stays true of a designated roster.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- All four unavailable exits 2 with no judge spawned and no Finished File — **instantly**, not
  after four timeouts. This is `RUN-15`'s existing rule firing on the new arm, not separate
  behaviour, which is why it has no ticket of its own.
- The Manager can tell "did not run" from "crashed or timed out" by reading the Feedback File
  alone. Grep `PRM-2` for both literals.
- Before writing that a clause landed, `grep` for its identifier. A decision gets its identifier
  when it is accepted (`AGENTS.md`).
close_reason: RUN-15 third arm + zero-survivor counting both kinds of down; RUN-7/RUN-8/DIR-4/PRM-2/CONTEXT.md amended; CNF-27 added incl. the mixed abort case. Six gates exit 0; suite 18/7 against rloop-bash (CNF-11/12 join the reds because PRM-2 changed). F13 records that the Lean pair proves the failure arm only. 'All four unavailable' is unreachable - no codex probe - and RUN-15 is left unscoped because mixed down states are reachable.

title: Availability as a scenario axis: the six cases (#3)
description:
Add availability as an axis in the scenario alphabet and generate the six cases #3 requires
before any of this is trusted. This is the ticket that grows the enumeration.

Depends on the panel-membership-in-trace ticket (the trace needs somewhere to put membership) and
on the record-omitted-reviewer ticket (the behaviour has to exist to be enumerated).

## Why separate from the prefactor

Making membership visible does not grow the alphabet: under today's requirements every Panel is
the same four Reviewers, so membership is a constant. Enumerating *availability* multiplies the
generated set, so it belongs with the requirement change rather than with the mechanical
rewrite. Splitting them keeps a 206-row regeneration reviewable on its own.

## The six cases, from #3

1. One Reviewer unavailable — recorded, not spawned; the Run continues with the rest.
2. All four unavailable — exit 2, no judge spawned, no Finished File.
3. A Reviewer re-admitted in a later Round, once the fake reports capacity again.
4. A probe that fails — fail open, the Reviewer is spawned.
5. A probe whose output does not parse — fail open, the Reviewer is spawned.
6. An unrecognised model name — fail open and loud, not a silently smaller Panel.

Cases 4–6 are the fail-open paths. They are the ones that make the rule falsifiable; without
them "fail open" is a sentence nobody can check.

## What to change

- Availability as an axis in `tools/formal/Rloop/Scenarios.lean`'s alphabet.
- `python3 tools/check_scenarios.py --write`, then commit what it writes.
- The fakes in `conformance/` gain a way to report exhaustion and to report capacity again.
- `conformance/scenarios.tsv`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- Each of the six cases fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate the
  failure for each; a scenario that passes both ways tests nothing. This is the lesson `F5`
  already paid for — *"a check and its subject built from one misreading agree with each other"*.
- The row count grows, and the growth is reported in the commit message with the before and
  after.

## Lands next to

`F4` ("The scenario alphabet is a choice"). If this materially multiplies the set, say so in
`F4` — it is the finding that owns the size of the enumeration.

Case 2 is the reachable mixed form (RUN-21 gives no codex model a family). All eight mutants of rloop-bash go red after the same lines pass unmutated. title: PRM-4's clean-path shortcut swallows item 0 (#4)
description:
`PRM-4`'s report block contradicts itself on the clean path, and the contradiction is why a codex
Reviewer's bare `No findings.` carries no provenance. Fix the prompt; no vendor reasoning needed.

## The defect

Item 0 says *"Say 'I ran everything I needed' if that is true"*. The block then ends:

```
If there is nothing to report, write exactly: No findings.
```

`write exactly` names a literal, and it is the last and most specific instruction in the block. A
Reviewer with nothing to report is being told to emit that string and nothing else. The codex
Reviewers comply; `opus` is the one deviating by adding item 0 on top.

Evidence is on rloop-spec#4 (2026-09-21 comment): across seven Run Directories every bare report
is **exactly 13 bytes**, and every codex Reviewer that was itself blocked wrote item 0 in full —
including `sol`, which #4's original text reports as never complying.

## The change

In `03-prompts.md`, `PRM-4`, replace the closing line of the report block with:

```
If you have nothing for items 1 and 2, write item 0 and then exactly: No findings.
```

Keeps the literal that makes a clean report machine-recognisable; stops it swallowing item 0.

Then `python3 tools/check_fixtures.py --write`. Never edit `conformance/fixtures/` by hand
(`AGENTS.md`). A prompt is changed in `03-prompts.md` and nowhere else.

## What follows in the Implementation

`PRM-4`'s bytes are normative (`OVR-2`), so `rloop-bash` changes its hardcoded prompt and bumps
its `spec/` pin, then `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop` must pass. That is `ADR-0001`'s
designed path, not an accident of it. `CNF-11`/`CNF-12` compare the hardcoded prompt to the
fixtures byte for byte, so a missed byte fails the suite rather than going live.

## What does not change

`conformance/run` lines 164 and 320 compare a Feedback File to `"No findings."` exactly, but those
are **fake** Reviewers' canned outputs testing rloop's pass-through plumbing. A fake does not read
a prompt. Leave them.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `grep -n "No findings" 03-prompts.md` shows the literal in exactly one place, inside the new
  sentence.
- The regenerated fixture for `PRM-4` matches the document; `check_fixtures.py` proves it.
- In `rloop-bash`: `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop` passes against the bumped pin.

## Verification is a live observation, not a suite item

Only a live Run shows whether the reworded block is followed — the Suite proves the prompt was
*sent*, never that a model obeyed it (`00-overview.md`, *How much to trust this*). Record it as a
`CNF-22` observation with the next release, against a specific prediction: **a clean codex report
carries item 0 and the literal both.** If it still emits 13 bytes, the cause was not the shortcut
and #4's option 2 — telling the Manager in `PRM-2` to weigh a report with no item 0 — is next.
close_reason: Accepted exact PRM-4 amendment and regenerated fixture in Round 1; Manager verified byte preservation and all specification gates PASS. Remaining Implementation adoption tracked in rl-bvz; live observation tracked in rl-vgy.

title: Restatement check plus the ported citation gate (F2, #11)
description:
Catch a rule restated outside its home. `F2`'s trigger fired: one pull request produced eight
findings of one rule living in more than one place, in a set of 102 requirements that six gates
call green. Decided 2026-09-21 on rloop-spec#11; `F2` records the decision.

## Two parts, and they compose

**1. The restatement check, in `tools/check_ids.py`.** That file already parses every requirement
definition (`DEF_RE`) and every citation (`CITE_RE`) across the root documents and the ADRs, so
this is an addition to an existing pass, not a new gate:

> A line that cites another requirement's identifier while carrying an RFC-2119 keyword of its own
> must either be that requirement's own definition, or carry the owner's words verbatim in
> backticks.

The verbatim-quote exemption is not a new concession — `AGENTS.md` already demands it: *"**Quote
the sentence.** A claim about what another requirement says carries that requirement's own words
in backticks."*

**Probed 2026-09-21: 8 lines in the whole set.** Reviewable in one sitting. Two of them
(`01-run-lifecycle.md:221`, `03-prompts.md:112`) already quote and clear themselves. At least one
is a real second normative copy: `01-run-lifecycle.md:23` — *"A lone Run MAY start on a dirty
tree; a Run inside a Sequence MUST NOT (`SEQ-4`)"* — states `SEQ-4`'s rule itself while citing it.
Triage all eight; each is either the home, a quote, or a defect.

**2. Port `check_citations.py` from provisiond-spec.** It is at
`~/projects/provisiond-spec/tools/check_citations.py`, 284 lines, with a `citation-baseline.json`
alongside it. It flags a quoted phrase attributed to a requirement whose body does not contain it
— which is exactly what makes part 1's escape hatch real rather than honour-system. Without it a
writer can claim to quote and be wrong, which is how drift instances 1 and 4 survived
`check_fixtures.py`: the fixture faithfully reproduced the wrong sentence.

Wire both into `tools/check-all.sh`, each exit code captured directly, never through a pipe.

## Deliberately not done

`check_obligations.py` stays deferred, recorded in `F2`. Of the eight instances the one obligation
finding was a paraphrase, not a duty assigned to another requirement's subject. Build it when an
instance of that shape appears.

## Two of #11's four shapes need nothing

Recorded so they are not rebuilt:

- **In an Implementation repository.** `rloop-bash`'s copy was deleted for a pointer
  (`ADR-0005`, douglaz/rloop-bash#7). Nothing left to drift, and no check in this repository could
  reach it anyway.
- **In non-normative prose.** `CONTEXT.md`'s example dialogue now uses no value this Specification
  owns — no identifier, no filename, no exit status. A survey of every example dialogue in the
  author's repositories found nine, of which rloop's was the only one naming a spec-owned filename
  and the only one restating identified requirements; the other eight already followed the
  convention with no rule and no gate. There is nothing systemic here to enforce.

What remains is shape 1, across files — which is the shape a machine can find, because both ends
name an identifier. Shape 2, a requirement contradicting itself internally, has no mechanical
catch and stays a review duty.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with every gate in
  `README.md`'s *Gates* table passing — the existing identifiers gate now carrying the
  restatement check, and the ported citation gate added beside it. *This read "eight gates"
  until 2026-09-22 and was wrong twice over: six plus one is seven, and a count written into
  prose is what `AGENTS.md`'s "Cite the list; let it hold the number" forbids. A Manager
  blocked the Run on the contradiction rather than choosing a reading (`RUN-19`).*
- The restatement check fails on a deliberately introduced second normative copy, and passes once
  that copy quotes its owner. Demonstrate both directions; a check that only ever passes tests
  nothing (`F5`).
- `check_citations.py` fails on a quote altered by one word. Demonstrate it.
- Every one of the eight lines flagged today is triaged: home, quote, or fixed.
close_reason: Accepted after Round 4: restatement and owner-only citation checks integrated; original probe triaged; all README gates and 41 citation controls pass. Formatting-normalization precision recorded separately; existing lexical limits accepted.

title: Probe shapes RUN-21 rules on and the suite never produces
description:
Two shapes of probe output `RUN-21` gives a rule for, and `conformance/run` never produces. Both
were found by reviewers reading `RUN-21` against `conformance/fakes/agent`, not by a red item —
the suite is green over them because the fake cannot express them.

## The two cases

1. **The aggregate line at 100%.** The fake's `clear` shape always writes
   `Current week (all models): 67% used`, and the `fable`/`opus` shapes write it at 67% too. So
   `Current week (all models): 100% used` — the likeliest real exhaustion, a whole account out —
   is never seen. `RUN-21` says it reads `unknown`, deliberately: *"no family is named in it,
   nobody has observed what the probe prints when a whole account is exhausted, and a rule written
   against an unobserved format is a guess."* That is a rule, and nothing tests it.

2. **Both families at 100% at once.** `fable` and `opus` are scripted one at a time. Two
   `unavailable` Reviewers in one Round is reachable in the real world the moment an account's
   Fable and Opus buckets are both spent, and it exercises what one family cannot: two Reviewers
   not called, `astra` and `sol` still called, `failed` reaching 2 and the Run still reaching its
   judge.

## What to change

- `conformance/fakes/agent`: an `aggregate` shape writing `Current week (all models): 100% used`,
  and a `both` shape writing Fable and Opus at 100% in one output.
- `CNF-26`: add the aggregate shape to its list of readings that leave every Reviewer `unknown`.
- `CNF-27`: add the two-unavailable case — `fable` and `opus` neither called and both recorded,
  `astra` and `sol` both called, the judge reached, the Run ending 0.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all gates PASS.
- Each new case fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate both; a case that
  passes either way is what this ticket exists to remove.
- `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop --self-check` still passes against `rloop-bash`, which

title: Split the gates into a blocking and an advisory tier (ADR-0007)
description:
Split the restatement and citation gates into a blocking tier and an advisory tier, as
`ADR-0007` decides, and state in `F2` which tier each form belongs to.

`ADR-0007` is the decision and owns the reasoning. This bead is the work.

## What blocks the build

Exactly these forms, where the ownership claim is explicit in the syntax rather than inferred:

**Every introducer form below binds only an adjacent quotation** — nothing but whitespace
between the introducer and the quote. This applies to forms 1 and 2 exactly as to form 3.
Intervening prose makes the attribution advisory, whatever punctuation introduced it
(`ADR-0007`).

1. an identifier followed by a colon;
2. a possessive — `` `RUN-16`'s `` ;
3. a quotation immediately after its introducer;
4. a parenthetical whose **ownership prefix** is identifiers and separators. The ownership
   prefix is the content before the explanatory marker `F2` already recognises, or the whole
   content when there is none. So `` (`RUN-16`, `SEQ-4`) `` blocks, and
   `` (`SEQ-4`; but see `RUN-16` …) `` blocks on `SEQ-4` while the words after the marker claim
   nothing — which is why the acceptance table below gives that sentence the blocking tier.
   Do **not** test the whole parenthetical content; that would make the second advisory and
   contradict the table.

**The enumerated introducing-phrase list starts empty.** `ADR-0007` allows such a list; adding a
phrase to it is a separate decision recorded in `F2`, not part of this work. Do not invent
members for it.

## What warns and does not block

Everything else the current scanner detects, including ownership inferred across unrestricted
intervening prose. It still runs and still reports; it does not fail the build.

A finding in this tier must be distinguishable from a blocking one in the output, and the
aggregate runner's exit status must not depend on it.

## Also required

- **Restore `docs/adr/0006-*.md`'s original wording**, `` the probe `AGT-18` states ``, replacing
  `` the probe from `AGT-18` ``. It was changed in `2e7dfb8` only to stop a gate objecting to
  correct prose. Confirm it is silent or advisory afterwards, never blocking.
- Check the rest of the Specification for sentences reworded for the same reason and restore any
  found. `2e7dfb8` is the commit to read.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with every gate in
  `README.md`'s Gates table passing.
- **Each of the four blocking forms has a control that fails when the attribution is false and
  passes when it is true.** Both directions, or the control proves nothing.
- **Each advisory form has a control asserting the behaviour that actually occurs** — the finding
  is reported and the exit status is unaffected. *Do not write a control asserting silence.*
  Closing one recognition route can re-open another: excluding a parenthetical from the citation
  route was measured to produce a `RESTATEMENT` finding instead, because `tools/check_ids.py`
  treats a span as covered only when an owner was found for it. Assert what happens.
- **A control covers the nearest-citation fallback** in `tools/spec_text.py`: a form the explicit
  recogniser declines can still be caught by that route, and the tier it lands in must be
  asserted, not assumed.
- These sentences, run through both gates, land in the tier `ADR-0007` gives them — verify each,
  and keep them as controls:

  | sentence | tier |
  |---|---|
  | `` `SEQ-4` says the rule is `<RUN-16's exact words>` (`RUN-16`). `` | advisory |
  | `` `SEQ-4` says nothing about `one session` (`RUN-16`). `` | advisory |
  | `` `<RUN-16's exact words>` (`SEQ-4`; but see `RUN-16` …). `` | blocking |
  | `` `<RUN-16's exact words>` (`RUN-16`, `SEQ-4`). `` | blocking |
  | `ADR-0006`'s restored sentence | not blocking |

- `F2` states which tier each form belongs to and points at `ADR-0007` for why. It does not
  restate the reasoning.
- `README.md`'s Gates table says which gates can fail the build and which only report.

## Not in scope

Teaching the scanner to parse relative clauses or any grammar beyond the four blocking forms.
Adding members to the enumerated introducing-phrase list. Narrowing the quotation-shape heuristic
on the inferred route — worth doing for advisory noise, but it is not this decision and
`ADR-0007` records why.

title: Refuse a Run whose Seat cannot answer (#3, ADR-0008)
description:
Refuse a Run whose Seat cannot answer, and catch a Manager that runs out mid-Run.

`ADR-0008` is the decision and owns the reasoning. This bead is the work. `CONTEXT.md` already
defines `Seat`; do not redefine it.

## What to change

**Amend `RUN-21`.** The Probe runs before the pick as well as immediately before each Round's
Panel. It records one `<seat>:<verdict>` line per Seat — `manager`, `implementer`, `fable`,
`opus`, `astra`, `sol`, in that order — in `probe-pick.md` before the pick and in `probe-<r>.md`
each Round. The verdict rule does not change: a Seat is `unavailable` only on the anchored
`Current week (<family>): 100% used` match with the family in the existing two-row table, and
`unknown` in every other case. A Seat whose model is outside that table is always `unknown`.

**Add `RUN-22`.** Two rules:

1. When `probe-pick.md` records the Manager's Seat `unavailable`, or the Implementer's Seat
   `unavailable`, rloop MUST exit 2 without spawning any agent, and MUST write to standard error a
   message naming the Seat, its model, and the reset the probe reported.
2. rloop MUST NOT make Round `r`'s judge call when `probe-<r>.md` records the Manager's Seat
   `unavailable`; it MUST exit 2. This precedes `RUN-11` rather than adding a row to it: that
   requirement decides `After every Manager call`, and a call that was never made is not one.

**Amend `DIR-4`.** Add `probe-pick.out`, `probe-pick.err` and `probe-pick.md`, written by rloop
before the pick. Restate `probe-<r>.md`'s entry as the per-Seat line.

**Amend `CONTEXT.md`'s `Probe` entry.** It scopes the Probe to a Round's Panel and to Reviewers;
both become false. Remove `preflight` from its avoided aliases — `ADR-0008` records why.

**The byte contract, already settled — do not treat it as open.** Every line of `probe-pick.md`
and `probe-<r>.md` ends with a newline, including the last, and a not-run Feedback File is
`REVIEWER NOT RUN (unavailable)` followed by a newline. `RUN-15`'s `and nothing else` means no
other content, not the absence of a terminator; say so where it is read. This is what rloop-bash
already writes — a not-run Feedback File measured 31 bytes on 2026-09-22 — so the change is to the
Specification and the items below, not to the Implementation. `CNF-25`, `CNF-26` and `CNF-27`
disagree about it today: one compares bytes, two use command substitution, which cannot see a
trailing newline. Align all three. This closes `rl-vcq`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate in `README.md`'s
  Gates table PASS.
- A conformance item for each of the two refusals, the Manager's Seat and the Implementer's Seat.
  **Each MUST assert that no agent was spawned**, not merely that the status was 2 — a Run that
  spawned a Manager and failed also exits 2, so a status-only check passes against an
  Implementation that ignores this entirely.
- A conformance item for the judge guard: a Run whose Round 2 probe records the Manager's Seat
  `unavailable` exits 2 with no `manager-judge-2.out` in the Run Directory.
- A control that a Seat whose model is outside the family table starts the Run, recorded
  `unknown`. Fail-open is unchanged, and this is what proves it.
- Every item above fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate the failure for
  each; an item that passes both ways tests nothing (`F5`).
- `CNF-24`–`CNF-27` updated to the per-Seat record and passing.

## Not in scope

Substituting a model for an unavailable Seat, under any flag — `ADR-0008` rejects it. A second
Probe guarding the Implementer on every Round; `ADR-0008` records it as available on its own merits
and not this decision. Validating a model name against a roster: a typo still hangs, and nothing
here decides it.

**Do not add a pick-time refusal for an empty Panel.** Four `unavailable` Reviewer verdicts are
unreachable — two of the four Reviewers are codex and the family table holds no codex model, so
they always read `unknown`. `ADR-0008` records why the arm was dropped, and `RUN-15` keeps the

title: The fake and the model disagree past a probe script's last shape
description:
The fake and the model disagree about what the probe prints in a Round past the last shape a probe
script names. Today nothing reaches that Round, so this is a trap for the next probe script rather
than a live defect; found by the Panel on Run `20260922T214422.432717855Z-3306563`.

- the fake falls through to `clear` rather than repeating the last shape, matching the model; or
- `probeReads`'s docstring (or the enumeration itself) states that a probe script MUST name a shape
  for every Round its cap allows, and something enforces it.

title: Placeholders inside INSTRUCTION are substituted (PRM-6 untested)
description:
Placeholder text inside the caller's `INSTRUCTION` must survive rendering literally. Neither the
suite nor its own renderer honours that today.

Found 2026-09-23 by a three-model review of rloop-bash `02c6206` (opus, astra and sol
independently). `PRM-6` requires `literal substitution of each {{NAME}} below with its value and no
other change`. An Implementation that substitutes placeholders in sequence, `{{INSTRUCTION}}`
first, then runs the remaining passes over the instruction's own text. Observed:

```
$ rloop 'Repair literal {{UNAVAILABLE}} and {{ROUND}} tokens'
# the Manager received:  Repair literal  and 0 tokens
```

**The suite cannot catch this as it stands.** `conformance/run`'s own `render()` (near line 139)
substitutes `{{INSTRUCTION}}` first and re-scans the result, byte for byte what rloop-bash does
at `bin/rloop:243`, so the expected prompt cascades identically and a new row would stay green.
Under bash 5.2+ `patsub_replacement` an unquoted replacement also turns `&` into the matched
text, on both sides. Fix the renderer first.

## What to change

1. **Amend `PRM-6`**, the rule's home: the render is one pass — a value substituted in is never
   re-scanned, so placeholder text inside a value survives literally. Add a dated italic note
   naming the cascade that motivated it. `CNF-12`'s prose cites `PRM-6`; it does not restate the
   rule (`AGENTS.md`: one rule, one home).
2. **Fix `conformance/run`'s `render()`** so no value is rescanned: render in one pass and quote
   every replacement (`"${P_X}"`). "Substitute `{{INSTRUCTION}}` last" is not enough — a Run
   Directory path holding `{{INSTRUCTION}}` (given with `--run-dir`) would then have the
   instruction substituted into it. Demonstrate that the fixed renderer, given an instruction
   holding `{{TASK_FILE}}`, `&` and `\` and a `--run-dir` path holding `{{INSTRUCTION}}`, produces
   both values' bytes unchanged.
3. **Add one Run to `CNF-12`** whose instruction contains placeholder names and the
   substitution-hostile bytes — at least `{{TASK_FILE}}`, `{{UNAVAILABLE}}`, a backslash, `&` and
   `%s` — and whose `--run-dir` path contains `{{INSTRUCTION}}` (the cyclic case), and assert the
   recorded pick prompt equals the fixture rendered with every value's bytes unchanged. Mind the block's structure: `prompts_ok` is snapshotted before the fourth
   Run (`conformance/run` near line 226), so a Run placed after the snapshot feeds no verdict.
   Put the new Run before it or include its result; `rl-aa4` touches the same lines and can be
   rebased either way.

The Implementation used for `F5` demonstrations is `/home/master/p/rloop-bash`
(github:douglaz/rloop-bash) at `02c6206`; use a scratch copy of its `bin/rloop` under `/tmp`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate PASS.
- With the fixed renderer, the row fails against rloop-bash `02c6206`, fails against a scratch
  copy that merely substitutes `{{INSTRUCTION}}` last (the cyclic case catches it), and passes
  against a one-pass scratch copy; demonstrate all three (`F5`).
- Corrupting only the new Run's recorded prompt turns `CNF-12` red (the verdict sees it).
- Every other prompt row is unchanged: the four fixtures are byte-identical to before.

## Not in scope

Escaping rules for the instruction — there are none, and none are wanted. `PRM-1`–`PRM-5`'s
text.
close_reason: Done in 9e77a81 and 70648f5: PRM-6 states the render is one pass with a dated note; conformance/run's render() walks the template once and never rescans a value; a hostile Run (instruction with {{TASK_FILE}}, {{UNAVAILABLE}}, {{ROUND}}, backslash, & and %s; --run-dir holding {{INSTRUCTION}}) joins CNF-12 before the prompts_ok snapshot and its argv joins CNF-11. Demonstrated on scratch copies of rloop-bash 02c6206: cascade red, INSTRUCTION-last red, one-pass green, backslash-dropped red; CNF-5 and CNF-20 were already red there. Four Reviewers, no findings; their hygiene nits went to rl-aa4. rloop-bash needs the one-pass renderer as its next instruction.

title: AGT-2 usage-error corners CNF-5 does not exercise: empty --run-dir, swallowed values, --=x, --auto=1, octal
description:

four of them.

Found 2026-09-23 by a three-model review of rloop-bash `02c6206` (astra, sol, opus). Depends on
`rl-zero-durations-9uy`, which amends the same sentence of `AGT-2` and the same `CNF-5` block:
land after it and rebase on its wording.

| invocation | what happened | rule |
|---|---|---|
| `--auto --run-dir ''` | Sequence ran: the check tests the value's emptiness, not the option's presence | `SEQ-3` |
| `--implementer-model --max-rounds 1` | the missing value swallowed `--max-rounds`; the Implementer got model `--max-rounds` | `AGT-2` missing value |
| `--=x` | rewritten to `--` `x`, which an option terminator accepted | `AGT-2` unknown option |
| `--auto=1`, `--help=x`, `--version=x` | a value given to a flag that takes none was accepted; `--auto=1` ran a Sequence with instruction `1` | no rule today — see below |

title: A duration of 0 is accepted by AGT-2 and unbounded under AGT-14; make it a usage error
description:

reads zero as unbounded, so a conforming-looking Implementation has no bound at all.

run past any bound; `--implementer-timeout 1 --kill-after 0` with a SIGTERM-ignoring fake never
sent SIGKILL. `timeout --help`: `a duration of 0 disables the associated timeout`.

title: A timed-out agent's SIGTERM-ignoring descendant outlives rloop's exit (AGT-15 untested)
description:
A timed-out agent's descendant that ignores SIGTERM can outlive rloop's exit; `AGT-15` forbids it
and no item forces the `--kill-after` SIGKILL.

Found 2026-09-23 by the astra reviewer on rloop-bash `02c6206`. `AGT-14` sends SIGTERM to the
call's process group, waits `--kill-after`, then SIGKILLs the group. `AGT-15`: `rloop MUST NOT
exit while any agent process it started … is running`. rloop-bash's reaper waits for the
`timeout` wrapper only, then abandons the group; with a Manager fake that spawned a
SIGTERM-ignoring child and `--manager-timeout 1 --kill-after 1`, rloop exited 2 at 1.04 s with the
child still alive (`child state when rloop exited: S`).

it spawned are gone before the judge starts`, spawned with `RLOOP_FAKE_GRANDCHILD=1` — but that
grandchild is a plain `sleep 300 &`, which the group's SIGTERM kills, so nothing makes rloop wait
out `--kill-after`. `CNF-18`'s prose claims `no process of the fake's group survives` while
`conformance/run` (near line 324) checks only the fake's own pid and sets no grandchild.

  before the judge starts. Add a Manager-timeout row (a sleeping pick under `--manager-timeout 1

  gone before the executable returns 2. Add the grandchild to `CNF-18`'s SIGINT path so its
  prose is true, with the same two-pid assertion.

  cannot stay a zombie and `kill -0` failing is sufficient; if a Reviewer shows otherwise, read

title: The suite runs on the host PATH, so an undeclared dependency (rloop-bash's cmp) is invisible; CNF-1's own list is wrong
description:
The suite runs the executable on the host's full `PATH`, so an undeclared runtime dependency is
invisible; rloop-bash ships without `cmp` and stays green. `CNF-1`'s own dependency sentence is
also false.

Found 2026-09-23 by the opus reviewer on rloop-bash `02c6206`. Its flake wraps `git`, coreutils
and util-linux, but `bin/rloop` decides `RUN-12`'s and `DIR-6`'s byte-identity with `cmp`, which is
diffutils. Under `nix run` on a host without diffutils, `cmp` exits 127, read as "the files
differ": the no-decision guard can never fire (`Rloop.no_decision_off_burns`, the witness
`RUN-12` names — five Implementers at a cap of five where one was required) and every Round's
`task.md` is set aside as interference (`DIR-6`). Reproduced with `PATH` cut to git + coreutils +
bash. CI never sees it because `writeShellApplication` appends to the caller's `PATH`.

This is a suite property, not an rloop-bash one: `CNF-1` promises the items are the definition of
conformance, and a dependency the Implementation forgot to declare is a conformance failure the
suite cannot currently produce.

Two things stand in the way and are part of this bead:

- `CNF-1` says the suite needs `bash, git, GNU coreutils, grep, sed and awk on PATH and nothing
  else`. It also uses `cmp` (diffutils; `conformance/run` in several places and
  `conformance/test-panel-trace`) and `find` (findutils; `conformance/run` near lines 86–88).
- "The directories of `sh`, `git` and coreutils" is not a restriction anywhere those share a
  directory (`/run/current-system/sw/bin` here, `/usr/bin` on an FHS host): `cmp` would come
  along. The restriction must be a private directory of symlinks to named tools.

**Settled here: the restriction applies to every executable invocation the suite makes**, not to
one item.

## What to change

1. Amend `CNF-1`'s dependency sentence to name `cmp` (diffutils) and `find` (findutils).
2. Amend `CNF-2`, which owns `PATH`: before running the executable the suite resolves the tools
   `CNF-1` names to absolute paths, builds a private directory of symlinks to exactly those
   names plus what the fakes need (`bash`, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `tr`, coreutils), and runs the
   executable with `PATH` = the fakes directory, then that directory, and nothing else. `cmp` and
   `find` stay available to the suite's own code by absolute path and are not in the executable's
   `PATH`. An executable that relies on anything more must carry it (a wrapper that prepends its
   own inputs, as a nix `writeShellApplication` does, satisfies this). Say why in an italic note,
   citing `RUN-12` and this incident.
3. `conformance/test-panel-trace`'s executable checks run the same way.

The Implementation used for `F5` demonstrations is `/home/master/p/rloop-bash`
(github:douglaz/rloop-bash) at `02c6206`; `nix build` there and use `./result/bin/rloop`, since
the wrapper's own `PATH` prefix is what this bead tests.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate PASS.
- Under the restricted `PATH`, rloop-bash `02c6206`'s `result/bin/rloop` goes red on `RUN-12`'s
  item and on `CNF-9` (via `rejected-*` files), and a scratch build whose flake adds
  `pkgs.diffutils` passes every item; demonstrate both (`F5`).
- The suite itself still runs on this machine under the restriction. The spec's CI is unaffected:
  it runs `conformance/test-panel-trace` without an executable and never `conformance/run`.

## Not in scope

Fixing rloop-bash's flake — that is its own repository's work, to be given to its next Run as an
instruction. Auditing other tools `bin/rloop` calls (`uuidgen` is util-linux and wrapped; `flock`,
`timeout`, `env` are coreutils or util-linux).

title: AGT-15: reap each call's process group after every call, not only on a timeout (settled: reading B)
description:
**Settled by the owner on 2026-09-26: reading B — rloop reaps each call's process group after
every call, not only on a timeout. Do not treat this as open.**

Background: `AGT-15` says `rloop MUST NOT exit while any agent process it started, or the Probe
(AGT-18), is running`, and `AGT-16` puts each agent in its own group `so that AGT-14 and AGT-15
reach every descendant`. `AGT-14` says what happens at a timeout (SIGTERM the group, wait
`--kill-after`, SIGKILL). Nothing said what happens to a process an agent leaves in its group when
the agent exits normally — a build, a server or a check it backgrounded (the habit `F16` records).
Under the old reading such a leftover keeps writing into the working tree while the Panel reviews
and the Manager commits, and outlives the Sequence. rloop-bash `02c6206` waits for the process it
spawned alone.

## What to change

- **Amend `AGT-15`** (or `AGT-14`, whichever owns the sequence; cite, do not restate): after every
  agent call and every Probe, once the process rloop started has exited, rloop MUST send SIGTERM to
  that call's process group, wait up to `--kill-after` seconds for the group to empty, then send
  SIGKILL to what remains — before the step that follows the call. The call's exit status is the
  spawned process's, unaffected by the reaping. A group that is already empty costs nothing: the
  wait ends as soon as the group does. Reviewers run concurrently; each Reviewer's group is reaped
  when that Reviewer exits. Add a dated italic note naming this bead and the hazard.
- **Extend `CNF-17`** (or a sibling item citing `AGT-15`) with a row where a healthy fake exits 0
  but leaves a SIGTERM-ignoring child in its group (the existing `RLOOP_FAKE_GRANDCHILD` knob with
  its ignore-TERM mode): both the fake's pid and the child's are gone before the next step starts,
  and before the executable returns. Cover at least one Manager call and the Implementer.
- Check whether the formal model (`tools/formal/`) says anything about the call's lifetime; it
  probably does not, and then nothing changes there.

The Implementation used for `F5` demonstrations is `/home/master/p/rloop-bash`
(github:douglaz/rloop-bash) at `02c6206`; use a scratch copy of its `bin/rloop` under `/tmp`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate PASS.
- The new rows fail against rloop-bash `02c6206` and pass against a scratch copy that reaps the
  group after each call; demonstrate both (`F5`).
- `CNF-16`'s concurrency timing and `CNF-17`'s existing bounds still hold against the reaping
  scratch copy: a clean exit adds no wait.

## Not in scope

Processes that leave the group (`setsid`); `AGT-14` is about the group and says so. rloop-bash's own
change, which is its next catch-up Run's work.

title: test-panel-trace and fake-header nits from the rl-rounds-fallthrough-a5n Panel: the header's omitted-field claim; one-assertion F5 control; a control red for any reason; no Round 1 guard on the opus probe arm
description:
Suggestions from the Panel of Run 20260925T074815.482543987Z-2268035
(`rl-rounds-fallthrough-a5n`, commit `035644f`). Nothing is red: all four Reviewers reported no
findings, the gates exit 0 and the suite's verdict against `rloop-bash` `02c6206` is unchanged.
Every item below is in `conformance/test-panel-trace` or `conformance/fakes/agent`.

1. The header entry overreaches on one of its two cases (opus). `conformance/fakes/agent:11-15`
says a Round past the last group **and** a field its group omits give the failing defaults,
`which is what Scenarios.lean's behaviour defaults to there`. That is exact for the first case
and not for the second: `behaviour` indexes whole `RoundChoice`s, so the model has no
partially-scripted Round to default. The commit message has it right — "the model has no
representation for a partially-scripted Round" — and moving that clause into the header makes
the two homes agree.

2. The F5 control proves one assertion of three (fable, opus). The scratch copy restores all
three old defaults at once and `rounds_case` dies at its first failed `assert_equal`, so the
control never reaches the Reviewer or the judge assertion. Both Reviewers built single-site
restorations by hand and each was red at its own assertion (`o:-ok` -> `Round 2 Implementer`,
`p:-all` -> `Round 2 Reviewer`, the judge default removed -> `Round 2 judge`), so the teeth are
there; the file does not prove it. A loop over three single-site `sed` copies would, at about
the same length.

3. The control accepts any non-zero exit as red (opus). `conformance/test-panel-trace:159`,
`( rounds_case "$work/old-defaults" ) 2>/dev/null && die …`: a `chmod` that did not take or a
`sed` that produced an unparseable script also exits non-zero and leaves the control green while
proving nothing — the failure mode `probe_case`'s `cmp -s … && die 'the mutation changed
nothing'` guards against. Capturing the message and matching it against `FAIL: Round 2
Implementer*` closes it in the same line count.

4. The widened probe arm has no Round 1 guard (opus). `:116` asserts the `fable` shape differs
from `clear`, which is what makes `:117` mean something; nothing asserts the same of `opus-1`.
If the `opus` shape ever collapsed onto `clear`, `:124` would misfire with `Round 3 repeats the
script's last shape` instead of naming the real breakage. One `cmp -s "$work/probe/opus-1"
"$work/probe/clear" && die 'Round 1 of opus writes clear'` makes the two arms symmetric.

5. `Round 2 judge wrote a Finished File` has no mutant (fable). No restoration of the old
default reddens it: the old judge default wrote nothing and exited 0. The mutant would be a fake
that exits 1 after writing the file. Worth it only if F5 coverage is wanted per assertion rather
than per control; take or leave with item 2.

6. Take or leave (fable): `cmp -s late-3 opus-1 && die` at `:124` is implied by the two `cmp`
calls against `clear` (`late-3 = clear` and `clear != opus-1` already hold). The brief asked for
it in those words, so it is not wrong — only redundant.

Acceptance: whatever lands is demonstrated, not asserted — each new or changed assertion shown
red against a scratch copy (`F5`); `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0,
unpiped, with the two pre-existing advisories and no new one; `conformance/scenarios.tsv` and
`conformance/run` unchanged; the suite's verdict against `rloop-bash` `02c6206` still
`19 passed, 11 failed` with the same eleven names.

title: Nits from the rl-probe-block-some-class-1fx Panel: positive()'s 'complete Panel' label on a three-member Panel; the header's mutation-site inventory; CNF-27's 'nothing else exercises the two kinds together'; narrowProbe's 'whatever the probe took out'
description:
Nits from the `rl-probe-block-some-class-1fx` Panel (opus, Run
`20260925T080910.224323832Z-2268035`, commit that closed it). Each is prose the change made
inaccurate; none affects a gate's verdict. Line numbers move — re-derive before editing.

- `conformance/test-panel-trace`, `positive()`: the helper hardcodes the word `complete Panel`
  into both its assertion label and its PASS line, because it was written for the three
  probe-unscripted lines whose Panel is all four Reviewers. The new `some`-with-an-uncalled-Reviewer
  control reuses it, so the gate prints `PASS: S210 complete Panel, exit 0, expected = observed:
  pick,impl1:ok,panel1:some:astra+opus+sol,judge1` — a three-member Panel announced as complete,
  contradicted by the trace three words later. The reuse is right; take the label as an argument,
  or drop the claim and say `expected = observed` alone.
- `conformance/test-panel-trace`'s header: `The mutants are pinned to rloop-bash's source, its two
  literal Reviewer loops in do_round and its probe reading (RUN-21)` now enumerates one site short.
  The new mutant pins a third, the zero-survivor abort `[ "$failed" -lt 4 ]`, and its replacement
  text also depends on the `pids` array's literal shape. The header is what tells a reader why the
  argument must be the rloop-bash script and what breaks when rloop-bash moves.
- `conformance/run`, the `rec-omitted-abort` block of `CNF-27`: `Nothing else exercises the two
  kinds together` is now false on a strict reading — the generated probe block reaches a Round with
  an uncalled Reviewer beside a failed called one (`S209`, `S210` and their kin). What the sentence
  is really claiming is that nothing else makes the two kinds *all down* together, which is still
  true; narrow it to that.
- `tools/formal/Rloop/Scenarios.lean`, `narrowProbe`'s docstring: `.some` is "not all down
  **whatever the probe took out**". `Loop.lean`'s `allDown` is `called.isEmpty || p == .none`, so a
  probe that took every Reviewer out would be all down. True for `probeReads`, which can remove
  only `fable` and `opus`, but the condition is `while some Reviewer is still called` and saying so
  costs nothing.

`conformance/test-panel-trace`'s new lines are also 168 and 113 columns where the file wraps near
100; `rl-0pj` owns that file's width nit and says to re-derive with `awk 'length>98'`, so these
fall to it rather than here.

title: README's Gates lead-in says CI runs the gates on every push; the workflow runs on master/main pushes, pull requests and dispatch
description:

Whole-README, low priority. Prose only: the workflow's triggers are not in scope, and rl-5mk owns
its last step.
close_reason: README.md:16-17 now names .github/workflows/gates.yml as the runner instead of claiming every push; no trigger list mirrored in prose (cfcf6e9). Gate green.

title: CNF-23 reads one judge argv where the item asserts every; head -1 would miss a retried judge call
description:
Suggestions from the Panel of Run `20260925T090746.368477655Z-2268035` (`rl-csw`), raised by the
opus Reviewer. Nothing is red; both are reach gaps that Round's accepted narrowing made visible.

That Round settled `CNF-23`'s pass message against the read rather than the other way round: the
message now says `the one Round's judge call carries it` (`conformance/run`), which is true of the
scenario, scripted `RLOOP_FAKE_ROUNDS="impl=ok;panel=all;judge=done"` — one Round, one judge
argument list.

1. `06-conformance.md` `CNF-23` asserts `every judge call is given that same id`, and the suite now
   says out loud that it reads one. In a one-Round Run the two coincide, so nothing is unverified
   today, but no `CNF` item exercises the property over a Run with more than one judge call. The
   cheap close: script a second Round, loop over every `*-manager-*.argv` whose round is at least 1,
   and let the pass message say `every judge call` again.
2. `conformance/run`'s read is `ls "$rec"/*-manager-1.argv … | head -1`, the first match. The fake
   prefixes each record with a sequence number (`conformance/fakes/agent`), so an Implementation
   that retried a judge call would write two `*-manager-1.argv` files and only the earlier one would
   be read — under which even the narrowed message overclaims. Pre-existing, and reachable only by
   an Implementation doing something no requirement permits; recorded so it is not rediscovered.

Whichever shape is taken, item 1's loop subsumes item 2's `head -1`.

Also noted and **not** filed: the same Reviewer read `Of standard error the item asserts presence
only.` in `CNF-29` as having lost the colon that made the two following sentences its support
(`presence only, because …` was the offered shape). Taste; the substance is intact and the two
quotations' blocking attribution shapes depend on what follows the verb, not on that punctuation.

message describes what the suite reads; the suite's verdict list does not move except for that
message.

title: CNF-11's 'every judge call carries that same id' is a second home for CNF-23's property; CNF-23's prose does not name its two-Round shape
description:
Suggestions from the Panel of Run `20260925T092734.145398704Z-2268035`
(`rl-cnf23-every-judge-argv-zq6`, commit `9159dc8`), raised by the opus Reviewer. Nothing is red:
the gates exit 0 and the suite's verdict against `rloop-bash` `02c6206` is `19 passed, 11 failed`
with the eleven names it had before. All three are prose or reach, in `06-conformance.md` and
`conformance/run`.

1. `CNF-11` carries a second home for a property `CNF-23` owns. `06-conformance.md`
   `CNF-11` says the pick's `<session id>` is the `session` file's content `and every judge call
   carries that same id`; `CNF-23` says `every judge call is given that same id` and is the
   requirement's home — it is the item that now reads them all (`conformance/run`, the loop over
   every `*-manager-[1-9]*.argv` of the third argv Run). `CNF-11`'s block still reads one judge
   call per Run, and the third Run now makes one it does not read, so the sentence over-describes

   sets the precedent for naming a shape in the item: `A Run of two Rounds leaves probe-pick.*,
   probe-1.* and probe-2.* and no probe-0.*`. One sentence either way; take it with item 1, since
   both are the same document's prose about the same Run.

3. Recorded, not a defect: `conformance/run`'s `check_call` reads `recf=$(ls $1 2>/dev/null | head

   requirement permits; `:422`, `:551`, `:555`, `:589` and `:663` read the same way. Noted by the

title: CNF-11 and CNF-23 wording nits from the rl-cnf11-judge-id-second-home-93a Panel: 'sends the brief back' where the document says 'rewrite'; 'reads them all' without CNF-23's codex scope
description:

(`rl-cnf11-judge-id-second-home-93a`, commit `62aad4c`), raised by the opus Reviewer. Nothing is

title: No item reads a --manager claude Run's Round 2 judge call for the session id (RUN-16 reach, sibling of rl-csw)
description:
Raised by the opus Reviewer of Run `20260925T095253.818886783Z-2268035`
(`rl-cnf11-judge-id-second-home-93a`, commit `62aad4c`). Nothing is red; this is reach, and the
sibling of `rl-csw`, which closed the same gap for the codex preset.

`RUN-16` covers both presets: `The Manager MUST be one session for the whole Run: the pick
establishes it, every judge call resumes it (`AGT-3`, `AGT-4`), and rloop MUST write its id to the
`session` file (`DIR-4`)`. The only place the suite reads a Round 2 or later judge argument list
for the session id is `CNF-23`'s loop over `"$rec"/*-manager-[1-9]*.argv` (`conformance/run:335`),
and that Run is a `--manager codex` Run. The other reads of a later judge record check something
else: `conformance/run:357` is `CNF-13`, which greps the base hash out of the prompt, and `:759` is
`CNF-30`, which checks only that no Round 2 judge argument list exists. `CNF-11`'s block reads each
Run's Round 1 judge record alone.

So under `--manager claude` an Implementation that resumed Round 2 under a different id than the
`session` file's would pass the suite. The reach was always this; what commit `62aad4c` changed is
that `CNF-11`'s prose no longer covers for it — it now says what it reads, which is the Round 1
call.

The question this opens is which item should own the claude preset's every-judge-call reading.
`CNF-11` reads argument lists per role and would have to grow a loop; `CNF-23` is the
codex-session item by its own first clause and is the wrong home; a third item, or a widened
`CNF-11` clause plus its loop, are the candidates. Whoever takes it decides that first, then
writes the reading, then gives the item a shape that names the Round count as `CNF-23` and
`CNF-24` now do.

Acceptance: an item of `06-conformance.md` reads every judge call of a `--manager claude` Run of
more than one Round and asserts each carries the `session` file's id; `nix develop --command bash
tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with the two pre-existing advisories and no new one; the
suite's verdict against `rloop-bash` `02c6206` is recorded before and after, and any change in it
is explained.
close_reason: Landed in commit 0e74dbc, one Round. The Consultation (opus and astra, both answering, both choosing B; fable out of quota and counted as not answering) settled the item's home: CNF-33, a default-preset sibling of CNF-23, rather than a widened CNF-11. CNF-33 runs a Run of its own — no --manager flag, two Rounds, Round 1 judging rewrite and Round 2 done — reads both judge records for the session file's id, names the Round count and fails on one record or none; CNF-11's pointer now names both preset owners. Gate exit 0 unpiped with the two standing advisories and no new one; suite against rloop-bash 02c6206 moved 19 passed, 11 failed to 20 passed, 11 failed with the same eleven names, CNF-33 green there because that build carries the resume id correctly and is red on CNF-11 over the judge call's other arguments. Seen red on scratch copies for a wrong id, a one-Round Run and an empty glob. The Panel's nits are rl-cnf33-panel-nits-agj and rl-grep-fixed-string-session-id-113.

title: CNF-33 and CNF-11 nits from the rl-claude-judge-session-id-reach-a1j Panel: a false reason in the non-empty-id guard's comment; the pointer's 'every judge call of a Run'; an orphan line
description:
Suggestions from the Panel of Run `20260925T101213.513558317Z-2268035`
(`rl-claude-judge-session-id-reach-a1j`, commit `0e74dbc`): item 1 from the astra Reviewer, items
2 and 3 from the opus Reviewer. Nothing is red — the gates exit 0 with the two standing advisories
and the suite against `rloop-bash` `02c6206` is `20 passed, 11 failed` with the eleven names it had
before, `CNF-33` green.

1. `conformance/run:836`-`:837`. The comment above `CNF-33`'s non-empty-id guard reads

   > a non-empty id before the comparison: `grep -qx` over an empty one matches the trailing empty
   > line every NUL-terminated argument list ends with

   and the reason is false. `tr '\0' '\n'` turns the record's final NUL into the last line's
   terminator, not into an empty line: over `claude\0-p\0prompt\0--resume\0abc\0`, `grep -qx -- ''`
   exits 1. An empty line appears only when the argument list holds an actual empty argument
   (`a\0\0b\0`), where `grep -qx -- ''` exits 0. The Manager confirmed both. The guard is worth
   keeping — an empty `session` file gets its own detail instead of two `does not carry the id`
   lines — so replace the reason, do not delete the guard.

2. `06-conformance.md:103`. `CNF-11`'s new pointer reads `every judge call of a Run is read by
   CNF-23 under --manager codex and by CNF-33 under the default preset`. It is strictly better than
   the `is the item that reads them all` it replaced, and it closes item 2 of
   `rl-cnf11-cnf23-wording-nits-8m1`, but it still parses as a claim about any codex Run, where each
   item reads the one Run it asserts and `CNF-33`'s Run is not one of `CNF-11`'s. The opus Reviewer
   offers `the item that reads a Run's judge calls all is CNF-23 under --manager codex and CNF-33
   under the default preset`, which owns the ownership claim alone.

3. `06-conformance.md:104`. The pointer's edit left a 19-character orphan line mid-paragraph.
   Reflow it. The same item is already ragged at `:108`, so this changes nothing that matters and
   is worth doing only alongside item 2.

Acceptance: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with the two
pre-existing advisories and no new one; no requirement and no suite behaviour changes; the suite's
verdict against `rloop-bash` `02c6206` is still `20 passed, 11 failed` with the same eleven names.
notes:
2026-09-25, from the Panel of Run 20260925T104239.796514290Z-2268035 (rl-grep-fixed-string-session-id-113):
item 1's comment is now stale in a second way. The comparison nine lines below it is `grep -Fqx`
since that Run, so the comment's `grep -qx over an empty one matches the trailing empty line` names a
flag the block no longer carries as well as giving a false reason. Both Implementers left it
deliberately -- renaming the flag inside a false sentence makes the comment look maintained without
making it true. Whoever takes this item rewrites the reason and the flag in one edit.

The `-F` change does not affect the guard's need: `printf 'a\0b\0' | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -qx -- ''`
and the same with `-Fqx` both exit 1, and `printf 'a\0\0b\0' | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -Fqx -- ''` exits
0, so an empty pattern still matches only an actual empty argument, either way.
close_reason: The CNF-33 guard comment now states the mechanism that makes the guard load-bearing: a judge record carries the rendered PRM-2 prompt, whose blank lines survive tr '\0' '\n', so grep -Fqx -- '' matches and, without the guard, an empty session id would read as carried by every judge call and CNF-33 would pass green. The guard does not suppress the loop's per-call misses - it falls through to the loop - and the earlier close reason on d6be5a7 and the body of f357606 both repeat that false claim. Commit 2a8d78d carries the correction. Items 2 and 3 (06-conformance.md CNF-11's pointer and the reflow) landed in f357606 and are unchanged. Gates exit 0 with the two standing advisories; the suite against rloop-bash 02c6206 is 20 passed, 11 failed with the same eleven names and CNF-33 green.

title: CNF-33's and CNF-23's session-id comparison is grep -qx, so the id is a regex, not a string
description:
Raised by the opus Reviewer of Run `20260925T101213.513558317Z-2268035`
(`rl-claude-judge-session-id-reach-a1j`, commit `0e74dbc`). Nothing is red; this is reach.

Both session-id readings compare the id with `grep -qx -- "$sid"`, which treats the id as a basic
regular expression rather than as a string: `conformance/run:846` (`CNF-33`) and
`conformance/run:369` (`CNF-23`).

Under `--manager codex` the id is the fake's own hardcoded UUID and `CNF-23` compares it against
that literal first, so nothing the Implementation chooses reaches the pattern. `CNF-33` is the
first place it does: under the default preset `AGT-3` says the pick MUST be
`claude -p <pick prompt> --session-id <session id> …` with an id `RUN-16` says is `one rloop chose
before the pick`, and `CNF-33` reads whatever that Implementation wrote to `session`. An
Implementation whose `session` file held `.*` would pass `CNF-33` vacuously — it would fail
`CNF-9`, which requires the file to hold `the Manager's session id as a UUID`, so no conforming
Implementation is at risk and nothing is red today.

`grep -Fqx` is one flag, inside `CNF-1`'s toolbox, and makes the comparison the string equality
both items' prose describes. Whoever takes it should decide first whether `CNF-23`'s line moves
too — the two lines are identical and leaving one behind is the kind of split this repository files
tickets about — and whether either item's prose needs to say the comparison is of bytes, or whether
the existing wording already carries it.

title: CNF-33 and CNF-23 compare the session id against lines, not arguments; the judge prompt's blank lines make the non-empty-id guard load-bearing
description:
Raised by the fable Reviewer of Run `20260925T113156.309844349Z-2268035`
(`rl-cnf33-panel-nits-agj`), and independently by the Manager while judging it. Nothing is red;
`CNF-33` is green against `rloop-bash` `02c6206`. Filed so it is not rediscovered from scratch.

`CNF-33` (`conformance/run:843`-`:847`) and `CNF-23` compare an argument list against the session id
by flattening the NUL-separated record and matching whole *lines*:

```
tr '\0' '\n' < "$f" | grep -Fqx -- "$sid"
```

The line model is not the argument model. A recorded judge call carries the rendered `PRM-2` prompt
as one argument, and that argument holds newlines -- `conformance/fixtures/prompts/PRM-2.txt` has
seven blank lines. So after `tr` a judge record has blank lines of its own, and the comparison is
matching lines *inside* an argument, not arguments.

Two consequences, both currently harmless:

- An empty `sid` would match one of the prompt's blank lines, so every judge call would read as
  carrying the id and `CNF-33` would pass green. Only the non-empty-id guard at `:838` stops that;
  the guard is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Verified:
  `printf 'claude\0-p\0%s\0--resume\0abc-123\0' "$(cat conformance/fixtures/prompts/PRM-2.txt)" |
  tr '\0' '\n' | grep -Fqx -- ''` exits 0.
- A session id is a UUID (`RUN-16`), so nothing else in a record can equal one line of it by
  accident. The false-positive risk is theoretical, not present.

GNU `grep -zFqx -- "$sid" "$f"` compares whole NUL-terminated arguments and drops the `tr` entirely,
which would make the assertion mean what it reads as and leave the guard purely cosmetic. `-z` is
a GNU extension; `CNF-1` owns the suite's toolbox and would have to be checked before relying on it.

This is a suite behaviour change, not a comment fix, so it does not belong to
`rl-cnf33-panel-nits-agj`. Worth doing alongside `rl-rmg`, the other open sweep of this file's
`grep` calls.

Acceptance, if taken: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with the two

becomes, an empty `session` file still makes `CNF-33` fail, demonstrated.

description:

Pinning it costs one more invocation: run the subshell with its working directory at the scratch
root and a *relative* thin entry on `PATH`, then assert the private directory's link for a name
like `sed` is still absolute. The existing `readlink`/`case` assertion is already in place to
catch it.

title: The relative-entry CI control's mutant reds both trees: swap it for the narrow one that only the retargeted read catches
description:
`.github/workflows/gates.yml:152-163`, *Prove the panel-trace gate can fail on a lost relative-entry
normalisation*, applies the whole-line mutant
(`:157`: `sed -i '/a relative PATH entry prints a relative path/d' conformance/scenario-lib.sh`) and
then requires `grep -qF 'FAIL: a relative PATH entry: cat links to a relative path'` (`:162`, moved
from `sed` to `cat` in `37f8fce`).

That mutant deletes the whole normalisation, so every link made from a relative `PATH` entry dangles,
including the names `executable_path_needs` holds — the control was red on the pre-`6dc3326` tree too,
through the same read. It therefore re-proves what the group did before rl-rp-assert-unguarded-name-cgk
and not what that work bought.

The discriminating mutant, measured by the Round-2 opus Reviewer on a scratch copy of `37f8fce`
(unmutated exit 0; mutated exit 1 on exactly that line), normalises only the names the refusal walks:

    sed -i 's|case "$file" in /\*) ;; \*) file="$PWD/$file" ;; esac # a relative PATH entry prints a relative path|case "$file" in /*) ;; *) case " $executable_path_needs " in *" $name "*) file="$PWD/$file" ;; esac ;; esac|' conformance/scenario-lib.sh

The anchor matches exactly once in `conformance/scenario-lib.sh` (line 40). Against it the
pre-`6dc3326` reads on `sed` exit 0 and print the false
`PASS: restrict_path links absolutely what a relative PATH entry found relatively`, while the `cat`
reads exit 1.

Whether the narrow mutant replaces the control at `:157` or joins it as a second step is this issue's
call; a second step costs another ~629 MB scratch copy in CI.

Acceptance: the step(s) pass on a clean tree and fail when the relative-entry group's reads are put
back on a name `executable_path_needs` holds; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` and
`nix flake check -L` both exit 0 unpiped with the advisory set unchanged; no group, assertion or
message in `conformance/` moves.
close_reason: Done in 9d59bbe: the relative-entry control's mutant now normalises only the names executable_path_needs holds, so it reds the cat read 6dc3326 retargeted and leaves the pre-6dc3326 sed read green. It replaced the coarse mutant rather than joining it. Panel nits filed as rl-4vs.

title: The skip group asserts its exit status before its two link reads, so those reads can never be the only witness
description:
Deliberately declined in Round 1 of rl-rp-assert-unguarded-name-cgk, with reasoning the Panel
accepted; filed so the remaining half of that bead is not lost.

The skip group of `conformance/test-panel-trace` asserts
`assert_equal "$(rp_run "$rp_work" "$thin")" 0 'a name the host lacks: exit status'` (`:203`) before
reading the link it cares about (`:216-219`, `[ -L ]` and `readlink` on `sed`). The relative-entry
group below it has the opposite order on purpose — it captures the status at `:231` and asserts it
only at `:236`, after the reads (`:227-229` says why) — which is what let that group's reads become
load-bearing once they moved to `cat` in `6dc3326`.

Because `sed` is in `executable_path_needs` (`conformance/scenario-lib.sh:25`), anything that dangles
its link makes `restrict_path` exit 2 at `conformance/scenario-lib.sh:44-45`, and `:203` reds first.
Retargeting `:216-219` to `cat` alone buys nothing while `:203` runs first: the group builds its links
in one `ln -s` loop, so a defect that dangles `cat` dangles `sed` too.

Two parts, in this order: defer `:203` past the two reads the way the relative-entry group defers
`rp_rel_status`, then retarget `:216-219` to a name `executable_path_needs` does not hold (`cat`, as
the group below now uses). Either without the other is not worth doing.

Acceptance: a mutant that reddens the reads and not the status is named and measured red/green;
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` and `nix flake check -L` exit 0 unpiped with the
advisory set unchanged; `restrict_path`, `executable_path_needs` and `coreutils_programs` untouched;
no group or assertion added or dropped; and `.github/workflows/gates.yml`'s `grep -qF` controls still
name messages the suite prints (`:149` is the skip group's).
close_reason: Done in a45756e. The skip group's rp_run status goes into rp_skip_status and is asserted after the two link reads (conformance/test-panel-trace:207, :224), and those reads were retargeted from sed to cat (:220-222), a name executable_path_needs does not hold. Discriminating mutant, measured by the Implementer, by the opus and sol Reviewers and by the Manager on scratch copies: link only the names executable_path_needs holds (anchor 'ln -s "$file" "$private/$name"', exactly once in conformance/scenario-lib.sh) -- unmutated exit 0, mutated exit 1 with 'FAIL: a name the host lacks: cat is not a symlink in the private directory' first, before this group's PASS line, while against conformance/ at 0898ff7 the same mutant leaves the skip group green and reds the relative-entry group instead. check-all.sh exit 0 with the RUN-16 advisory alone; nix build --rebuild of checks.gates exit 0. gates.yml:149 still names a message the group prints. Remaining nits filed as rl-skip-group-readlink-comment-nits-suu.

title: gates.yml's grep controls can go stale: one AGENTS.md line (settled: shape A)
description:
**Settled by the owner on 2026-09-26: shape A, documentation only. Do not build a gate; do not
treat this as open.**

Background: `.github/workflows/gates.yml` holds `grep -qF <literal>` controls, each proving a

three ways (opus C, astra A, sol B); the owner chose A.

a silent cache hit: whoever rewords a message a gate or the suite prints greps
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` for the old text first and updates any control that quotes it, in
the same commit. The line must not claim to close the class — it describes a manual check (astra's
caveat).

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate PASS.
- `AGENTS.md` carries the line; nothing else changes: no workflow control, mutant or asserted

## Not in scope

A gate reading the workflow, source-line citations on the controls, message-template extraction.

title: Only the skip group's [ -L ] read is load-bearing; its readlink read cannot redden, and its new comment adds a reason to a pointer
description:
Leftovers from rl-rp-skip-group-order-h7w (`a45756e`), raised by the opus Reviewer as suggestions
and accepted as worth recording, not as edits to that commit.

**The `readlink` read still cannot be reddened by the code it pins.** The skipped-name group of
`conformance/test-panel-trace` now reads `cat` twice: `[ -L "$rp_work/private/cat" ]` (`:220`) and
`case "$(readlink "$rp_work/private/cat")" in /*)` (`:221-223`). Only the first became load-bearing.
The group's `PATH` entry is `$thin`, an absolute path (`:197`), so `type -P` never prints a relative
path under it and the normalisation at `conformance/scenario-lib.sh:40` is dead for this group.
Measured by that Reviewer, not assumed: the `.github/workflows/gates.yml:157` mutant
(`sed -i '/a relative PATH entry prints a relative path/d'`) leaves the skip group printing
`PASS: restrict_path leaves out what the host lacks, names it once, and links the rest` and reddens
the relative-entry group instead, which is the group that owns that property (`:222-229`). So one of
the two reads is decoration. Whether to drop it, or to leave the pair as one read of "linked, and
linked to somewhere" whose second half the group below covers, is this issue's call; dropping an
assertion was out of scope in the brief that added them.

**The comment attaches its own reason to a quoted fragment.** `conformance/test-panel-trace:202-205`
says the reasons are the relative-entry group's to own, quotes two of that comment's phrases
verbatim, and then supplies a third clause of its own — "so that a defect reaching both is reported
as the read and not as restrict_path's refusal" — where the owner's reason (`:227-229`) is specific
to a lost normalisation. The generalisation is true of this group, but it is a second sentence of
rationale standing next to a pointer that says the rationale lives elsewhere, which is what
`AGENTS.md`'s "One rule, one home; everywhere else points at it" rules out. Two smaller things in
the same comment: "Both of this group's link reads read cat" repeats the verb, and the first quote
