title: CNF-34 observes the next call, not the next step: a Checkpoint that runs before the Implementer is reaped is green
description:
`CNF-34` asserts that a call that exits 0 leaves neither its own process nor anything in its group,
but it can only observe at the **next call**, not at the next **step**. `AGT-15` says rloop reaps
`before the step that follows the call`, and `RUN-7` puts the Checkpoint (`DIR-6`) between the
Implementer call and the availability probe: `1. one Implementer call … 2. the Checkpoint (DIR-6);
3. the availability probe`. The fake writes `CALLS_ALIVE` only when another fake starts
(`conformance/fakes/agent`, the snapshot block), so an Implementation that runs the Checkpoint
while the Implementer is still alive, and reaps only before the probe, is green.

Found 2026-09-26 by the sol Reviewer on `3e334bb` and reproduced by the Manager. A scratch copy of
rloop-bash `02c6206`'s `bin/rloop` that reaps each call's group after the call (so `CNF-34` and
`CNF-17` are green), mutated so that `checkpoint "$r"` runs before `reap "$impl_pid"` and the probe
still follows the reaping, gives `21 passed, 11 failed` — `PASS CNF-34`, `PASS CNF-24`, byte-equal
to the unmutated reaping copy. The hazard is not hypothetical: `DIR-6`'s Checkpoint reads and
rewrites `task.md` and sets aside a `finished.md` an agent wrote, so a straggler writing those
files races exactly the step that is meant to repair them.

## What to change

- Observe the Implementer's own process at the Checkpoint boundary, not only at the next call. The
  Checkpoint is not an agent, so no fake can witness it; the `git` shim `CNF-19` already puts first
  on `PATH` is the only black-box witness of a Checkpoint, and `DIR-6` says which git commands it
  runs. Decide whether a shim that snapshots the recorded `PID` pids is worth its weight, or
  whether `CNF-34`'s prose should instead say **call** where it now implies step — the prose at
  `06-conformance.md` already says `among the calls alive when it started`, so the narrower reading
  may simply be the honest one to keep.
- Whatever is chosen, an isolated mutant must redden it: the Checkpoint-before-reap copy above,
  which leaves probe ordering intact and is green on `CNF-24`.

## Also record

The own-process assertion and `CNF-24` (`probe not after the Implementer`) cannot be separated by
any mutant the Round's Implementer, the opus Reviewer or the Manager could build: `CNF-24` orders
calls by the `NNN-` prefix each fake writes as it *starts*, so it cannot see whether the earlier
call's process had *exited*, yet any Implementation that holds a call's own process past the next
**call** necessarily overlaps their starts. The argument is reasoning, not measurement, and today it
lives only in `3e334bb`'s commit message; `07-open-findings.md` is where it belongs if it is kept.

The `manager-0` arm of `CNF-34`'s new loop has no mutant behind it — the Checkpoint and early-probe
mutants both redden the `implementer-1` arm. It is live code on the same predicate against a pid
later records do carry, so it is not dead, but nothing demonstrates it red.

## Not in scope

The second Checkpoint (`RUN-7` step 5) and the judge, unless the same witness covers them for free.

title: AGT-15's 'the step that follows the call' and RUN-21's record of the probe's verdicts: two readings
description:
`AGT-15` requires reaping a call's group `before the step that follows the call`
(`02-agents.md:224-234`). `RUN-21` (`01-run-lifecycle.md:67-75`) has, after each probe call:

> After each call it MUST record for every Seat exactly one verdict — `unavailable` or `unknown` —
> in `probe-pick.md` before the pick and in `probe-<r>.md` in Round `r` (`DIR-4`)

and `RUN-7` (`01-run-lifecycle.md:46-58`) lists item 3 as `the availability probe (RUN-21, AGT-18),
waited for before the Panel starts` — the record is inside `RUN-21`, not a separate item of `RUN-7`.

Two readings, and they require different behaviour of an Implementation:

- **A.** Writing `probe-pick.md` / `probe-<r>.md` *is* the step that follows the probe call, so the
  group MUST be reaped before that record is written. A straggler of the probe's group that races
  that record is then non-conformance.
- **B.** The record is part of `RUN-7`'s item 3, the probe step itself, so the step that follows is
  the pick or the Panel, and reaping any time before the next call conforms. A straggler may then
  legitimately race the record.

Surfaced by the Round 1 Panel of `rl-cnf34-reviewer-probe-rows-2mv` (the `sol` and `opus`
Reviewers), which is why `07-open-findings.md`'s `F17` cannot say whether the Probe row's two
boundaries belong in its list of boundaries read at the call that follows alone: under A they do,
under B they do not. `sol` measured the gap: a mutant that writes the availability record with the
probe's child alive and reaps before the next call leaves `CNF-34` green.

`CNF-34`'s Probe row reads each probe's boundary at the call that follows it and is correct under
either reading; nothing in the suite turns on the choice. What turns on it is whether a further
witness is owed — the watching straggler `RLOOP_FAKE_WATCH` already provides, polling for
`probe-pick.md`.

**This is the specification owner's call (`RUN-19`). Do not pick it until the owner has chosen A or
B; the choice belongs here.** Whichever is chosen, `AGT-15` or `RUN-21` says so in one clause and
`F17`'s list is settled with it.

title: The suite word-splits paths: a TMPDIR holding whitespace reddens CNF-13 and gives CNF-34 a false red
description:
The suite breaks on a `TMPDIR` whose path holds whitespace, in at least two places, and one of them
is a **false red against a conforming Implementation**.

Measured on 2026-09-27 by the Manager of the `rl-cnf34-reviewer-probe-rows-2mv` Run, against
`/home/master/p/rloop-bash/result/bin/rloop` (`02c6206`), `TMPDIR='/tmp/space dir'` versus the
default:

- `CNF-13` goes FAIL where it is PASS otherwise, with `[space lacks <sha>]` brackets — a path split
  on the space and read as a record name.
- `CNF-34` gains `[reviewer: 8 Reviewer records, not the Panel's four]` and the same for `probe-1`,
  from `panel=($(ls "$rec"/*-reviewer-1-*.env))` (`conformance/run:469`), which word-splits the
  filenames. On that executable `CNF-34` is red anyway; on a reaping Implementation this is the
  difference between PASS and a false FAIL. Reported by the `astra` Reviewer of that Run's Round 1
  Panel, which measured the helper directly (four fixture records, one space in the path: `count=8`).
- The two runs otherwise agree: `18 passed, 14 failed` against `19 passed, 13 failed`, `CNF-13` the
  only verdict that moved.

So the fragility is a pre-existing class, not the `CNF-34` change's, which is why that Round left it:
a suite that cannot run under such a `TMPDIR` at all is not made worse by one more site. Fix the
class, not one site. `CNF-1` says the suite needs `bash`, `git`, GNU coreutils, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`,
`cmp` and `find` `on PATH and nothing else` and says nothing about the shape of `TMPDIR`; either the
suite handles whitespace or `CNF-1` says it does not.

## What to change

- Sweep `conformance/run` and `conformance/scenario-lib.sh` for every expansion of a path that can
  hold whitespace — unquoted command substitution into an array or a `for`, unquoted `$work`,
  `$rec`, `$repo`, `$private`, `$fakes` — and fix each. Collecting a glob into an array directly

title: CNF-34's probe-0 own-process read is green against a deferred probe reap unless the probe call outlasts the record
description:
`CNF-34`'s Probe row reads the probe before the pick from the pick's record: the probe's own pid must
not be among `CALLS_ALIVE` when `002-manager-0.env` starts (`conformance/run:542-557`, `gone_by`).
Measured against a reaping scratch copy of rloop-bash `02c6206` under `/tmp`:

- A mutant that neither waits for nor reaps the probe until the next call has started, at both of
  `RUN-21`'s call sites, gives two brackets and no others:
  `[probe-0: 001-probe-0.env GRANDCHILD ... alive when 002-manager-0.env started]` — the **group**
  half of the read at the pick's boundary, which does catch the deferral there — and
  `[probe-1: 004-probe-1.env PID ... alive when 004-reviewer-1-fable.env started]`. The `probe-0`
  **own-process** half stays green under it: the probe fake exits before rloop reaches the pick.
- That own-process half goes red only with a further defect beside the deferral, and with the
  deferral narrowed to the probe before the pick: that one probe call's standard input left open
  (`AGT-12`), so the call itself outlasts the record rloop writes from it. Then
  `[probe-0: 001-probe-0.env PID ... alive when 002-manager-0.env started]` is the item's whole
  detail, with nothing else of the suite moving. Recorded in `07-open-findings.md`'s `F17`.

So the row's own-process half at the pick's boundary does not, on its own, catch an Implementation
that defers the probe's wait and reap past the pick: it needs the probe call to still be running when
the pick starts, and a fake that exits in milliseconds does not arrange that. A real agent call
always would, which is why this is the suite's gap and not the Implementation's. The group half is
what carries that boundary today.

## What to investigate

The fake documents `RLOOP_FAKE_SLEEP_PROBE` (`conformance/fakes/agent:20`, the generic
`RLOOP_FAKE_SLEEP_<ROLE>`), and the row setting it would make the call outlast the record without a
second defect. **Unmeasured**: the sleep happens after the fake spawns its SIGTERM-ignoring child
(`conformance/fakes/agent:133`, `:176`), so a slept probe's group read may change too — a call that
starts while such a probe is still running finds its `GRANDCHILD=` line where one that starts in the
window before `:133` does not — and a Run whose probe sleeps costs the suite that second twice.
Measure both verdicts on a scratch copy of the suite — green against the reaping copy, red against
the deferral-only mutant — before changing the row, and leave the row alone if the sleep moves any
other read.

Not this bead: the watching-straggler witnesses (rl-cnf34-remaining-boundaries-4lq) and the reading
of `AGT-15` against `RUN-21`'s record (rl-agt15-probe-record-step-taf).

title: F17 wording nits from the rl-cnf34-reviewer-probe-rows-2mv Round 3 Panel: the green-group-half reason is over-general, and a Round count in prose
description:

`F17` paragraph *Which of `CNF-34`'s own-process reads a mutant reddens* (`07-open-findings.md`). The

- `Both own-process brackets come with a green group half for one reason: the fake writes
  GRANDCHILDREN_ALIVE (conformance/fakes/agent:98) before it spawns the child that ignores SIGTERM
  (:133), so a call that starts while the probe is still running finds no GRANDCHILD= line in the
  probe's record` — true of the window the two measured brackets fell in, and not of `while the probe
  is still running`. A probe that outlives its own spawn has written the line: the fake's
  `RLOOP_FAKE_SLEEP_<ROLE>` sleep is at `conformance/fakes/agent:176`, after the spawn at `:133`,
  which is the shape rl-cnf34-probe0-read-fast-fake-8et marks unmeasured. Narrow the clause to the
  window — while the probe is still writing its record, before it reaches `:133` — so the paragraph

  that put a red `probe-0` group bracket in the same paragraph is what makes a reader test it.
- `no mutant of either Round reddens that half either` is a count of Rounds in prose, in a paragraph

  this bead's mutants — per `AGENTS.md`'s *Cite the list; let it hold the number*.
- `Besides each probe's, which the reading below leaves open, the boundaries observed only at the call
  that follows are …`: *besides* reads as *in addition to*, which is one of the two readings rather
  than neutral between them, and `the reading below` is singular where the same paragraph names
  `RUN-19`'s `two readings that lead to different behaviour`.
- `one further defect`, which follows the description of the deferral at both call sites, still
  invites reading it as *the same deferral plus one thing* — the misreport Round 3 removed. *one
  further defect beside the deferral* closes it.
- `the pick's boundary` means `probe-0`'s reap boundary, witnessed by the pick's record, in the first
  paragraph and the pick call's own reap boundary in the second. Both are established idiom; a reader
  crossing between them re-anchors.

title: conformance/run is not newline-safe: CNF-1's clause says a space or a tab for that reason
description:
`11f3001` gave `CNF-1` a clause promising the suite runs under a `TMPDIR` whose path holds
whitespace. A newline is whitespace and the suite does not survive one, so `3744925` narrowed the
clause to a space and a tab, the shapes that were measured. This bead records what the narrowing
leaves standing and why, so the class is not re-raised from scratch.

## The sites

Reported by the `astra` Reviewer of Run 20260927T012424.193377950Z-2394293's Round 1 Panel, widened
by its `opus` Reviewer in Round 2, and each figure below reproduced by that Run's Manager against
`/home/master/p/rloop-bash/result/bin/rloop` under `TMPDIR=$'/tmp/rv-nl\ndir'`:

- `record_of` (`conformance/run:467`) selects a record with `ls "$rec"/*-"$2".env | head -1`. The
  path is truncated at the newline, to `/tmp/rv-nl` for a scratch tree under
  `/tmp/rv-nl<newline>dir/`. **The truncated prefix is non-empty, so `record_of`'s own guard
  (`:468`) never fires and no `no record of` bracket is printed** — `grep -c 'no record of'` over a
  whole newline run is `0`. The damage lands downstream, where `gone_by` and `panel_records` read a
  path that does not exist: `[reviewer: rv-nl has no CALLS_ALIVE line]`,
  `[probe-0: rv-nl recorded no PID]`, `[probe-1: rv-nl recorded no GRANDCHILD]`.
- `spawn_count` (`conformance/run:32`) counts with `ls "$1"/*.argv | wc -l`, and counted one `.argv`
  file as two.
- Five further items go red from the same class, which is the measured extent of the conversion a
  future Round would have to make: `CNF-21` `[dirty between runs: exit 2, 2 picks]`
  (`conformance/run:684`), `CNF-24` `[the pick: 2 probe calls]` (`:711`, `:720`), `CNF-27`
  `[… judge was not given fable's Feedback File]` (`:815` truncates `jf`, read at `:830`), and
  `CNF-28` and `CNF-29` `[… the probe before the pick did not run once]` (`:850`).
- Totals: `14 passed, 18 failed` under a newline `TMPDIR` against `19 passed, 13 failed` under the
  default, a space and a tab. Newly red: `CNF-21 CNF-24 CNF-27 CNF-28 CNF-29`.

A space and a tab are safe in all of them, because neither terminates a line.

## Why it was not fixed

That Round's Consultation asked A — narrow the sentence, change no code — against B — keep it and
make `conformance/run` newline-safe, about 25 `ls`-into-`head -1`/`wc -l` selections and counts
converted to globs and arrays. `claude-opus-5` at xhigh and `gpt-6-astra` at high both answered A,
independently and for the same reason: no user is known to want a newline in `TMPDIR`, and each
rewritten site in the artifact every Implementation is judged by is a fresh chance to turn a red row
green or a green row red. `opus` added that if the rewrite is ever judged worth having it belongs in
its own bead, demonstrated under a newline `TMPDIR` against a stable baseline, rather than bolted on
to defend a sentence. This is that bead.

## What to change, if it is ever picked

Convert every line-delimited path selection and count in `conformance/run` to a glob into a variable
or an array, as `11f3001` did for the five word-splitting sites. Demonstrate it: a full suite run
under a `TMPDIR` whose path holds a newline reaching `19 passed, 13 failed` with the default run's
failed list, and the default run unchanged. The five items above are the demonstration's targets —
they are red today for this reason alone. Then `CNF-1`'s `A newline in it is not supported` sentence
goes and its path clause widens from a space and a tab to whitespace. A conversion with no
newline-`TMPDIR` run behind it is not evidence.

Take care constructing the `TMPDIR`: `$(printf '\n')` strips the newline, so `nl=$'/tmp/x\ny'` is
the shape that actually tests anything. A run against a path with no newline in it looks green and
proves nothing.

## Also noted, and weaker

The `opus` Reviewer of the Round 1 Panel observed that `CNF-1`'s clause has no automated guard in
this repository and cannot have one: every check of it needs an rloop executable, which `ADR-0001`
keeps out. It suggested running `tools/check-all.sh` under a whitespace `TMPDIR` in CI, and supplied
its own caveat — that covers `scenario-lib.sh`, `restrict_path` and `test-panel-trace`, which were
already clean, and not the `conformance/run` sites that actually drifted. Weigh that before building
it; the brief of that Round ruled such a control out as scope.

title: CNF-13 passes vacuously if none of its three record globs matches
description:
`CNF-13` reads the base hash out of three recorded argument lists
(`conformance/run:369-372`, after `11f3001`):

    for f in "$rec"/*-reviewer-1-fable.argv "$rec"/*-reviewer-2-fable.argv "$rec"/*-manager-2.argv; do

## What to change

is a red bracket, not a vacuous pass. `CNF-13` wants the same — each of the three records found, or

Per `AGENTS.md`, the new assertion needs an isolated mutant that reddens it and leaves the rest of
the suite alone, measured against `/home/master/p/rloop-bash/result/bin/rloop`, not argued. Note that
`CNF-13` is `PASS` on that executable today, so the baseline is a green item: a mutant that suppresses

description:
`CNF-34`'s Reviewer brackets come out in a different order between any two runs of the suite, and the
order is not evidence of anything. The `opus` Reviewer of Run 20260927T012424.193377950Z-2394293's
Round 1 Panel spent a full 75-second suite run plus a synthetic sort test ruling this out as a
regression of `11f3001`, which had converted `panel=($(ls …))` to a glob; it then asked that the fact

What it measured, both runs against `/home/master/p/rloop-bash/result/bin/rloop`:

- Before: the Panel's records were `005-…-fable 005-…-opus 006-…-astra 007-…-sol`. After:
  `005-…-astra 005-…-fable 005-…-opus 006-…-sol`. The **names** differ, not the sorter.

title: Nothing obliges an Implementation to handle a whitespace repository or Run Directory path, so the suite's verdict is TMPDIR-dependent
description:
`11f3001` gave `CNF-1` a clause about the **suite**: it runs under a `TMPDIR` whose path holds
whitespace. Nothing in the set says anything about an **Implementation** and a whitespace path.
Raised as a question by the `opus` Reviewer of Run 20260927T012424.193377950Z-2394293's Round 1
Panel, which recorded `grep -rn whitespace *.md` finding no such requirement.

The consequence it drew: the suite makes its scratch tree under `TMPDIR` and hands those paths to the
executable — the repository it runs in, the Run Directory, `--run-dir`, `--base`. So an Implementation
that mishandles a whitespace path is green under the default `TMPDIR` and red under a whitespace one,
and the suite's verdict on such an executable becomes `TMPDIR`-dependent. Nothing is broken today:
rloop-bash `02c6206` handles it, which is why the two runs of that Round agree, and `CNF-12`'s hostile
Run already drives a Run Directory path holding `{{INSTRUCTION}}`, so the family is not new.

**This is the specification owner's call. Do not pick it until the owner has chosen; the choice
belongs here.**

- **A.** The set requires it of an Implementation. Then it is a `RUN` or `DIR` clause — the repository
  path, the Run Directory path and the paths rloop renders into a prompt hold whitespace — and a
  `CNF` item asserting it, with the fake driving a repository whose path holds a space. `CNF-12`'s
  hostile Run is the pattern for adding one placeholder-hostile shape to an existing item.
- **B.** The set does not require it. Then `CNF-1`'s clause is about the suite alone, which is what it
  says, and what wants writing down is that an Implementation is not held to it — so that a future
  Reviewer measuring a `TMPDIR`-dependent verdict knows it is out of scope rather than a defect.

Under either choice, `CNF-1`'s clause stands as it is: it is the suite's own guarantee and does not
change.

title: F18 and CNF-1 wording nits from the rl-suite-tmpdir-whitespace-0or Round 3 Panel: the unscoped guard claim, 3744925's second wrong claim, 'A newline in it'
description:
Wording left by the Round 3 Panel of `rl-suite-tmpdir-whitespace-0or` (commit `b6576cc`, the `sol` and
`opus` Reviewers). None changes what any gate reports; all three were measured or read by the Manager

## Not in scope

The race itself (`rl-cnf34-bracket-order-race-note-1dj`) and making the suite newline-safe
(`rl-suite-newline-paths-deferred-mzc`). Both are open on their own terms.

title: CNF-13's record guard is the only one that rests on the unmatched glob's text, so nullglob would reopen the vacuous pass
description:
`CNF-13`'s new guard (`conformance/run:372`, commit `86152e6`) is the only one of the suite's four
record-glob guards that rests on a non-matching glob leaving `$f` the pattern itself:

    [ -e "$f" ] || { ok=0; detail="$detail [no record matching $(basename "$f")]"; continue; }

Under `shopt -s nullglob` the three-glob list at `conformance/run:369` expands to nothing, the loop
body never runs, and `CNF-13` is green again on `[ "$e" = 0 ]` alone — the vacuous pass that guard
was added to close. Its three siblings survive that setting because each counts matches outside the
loop rather than reading the unmatched pattern: `check_call`'s `recf` stays empty
(`conformance/run:236-238`), the two `judges` loops stay at 0 (`:346-352`, `:998-1002`), and
`panel_records` stays at 0 records, not four (`:474-478`).

Nothing under `conformance/` or `tools/` sets `nullglob` — `grep -rn 'nullglob\|shopt' conformance/
tools/*.sh` finds nothing — and `bash conformance/run` picks a `shopt` up only through `BASH_ENV`,
so this is durability against a later edit, not a defect today. Raised as a take-or-leave
suggestion by the `opus` Reviewer of Run `20260927T025548.846413425Z-2394293`'s Round 1 Panel, which
found no defects; the Manager verified the reading and declined it as larger than the Round's brief
asked for.

## What to change, if this is picked up

The siblings' shape: a `found` counter incremented in the loop and one check after it, so what
reddens the item is the count of records found rather than the text of an unmatched glob. That
loses the bracket naming *which* of the three is absent unless the check names them, so weigh the
diagnostic against the uniformity before writing it.

Per `AGENTS.md`, any change here needs its mutant measured against
`/home/master/p/rloop-bash/result/bin/rloop`, not argued: `CNF-13` is `PASS` on that executable, so
the mutant is a scratch copy of it under `/tmp` whose Round 1 `fable` Reviewer records under a tag
the glob does not reach, gated on `have_base` (`bin/rloop:163`, read as `${have_base:-}` — a bare
`[ "$have_base" = 1 ]` dies under the wrapper's `set -o nounset` and reddens two dozen items).

## Declined with it, so it is not re-raised

The same Reviewer noted that the bracket names a pattern rather than a record
(`[no record matching *-reviewer-1-fable.argv]`). That is unavoidable when nothing matched, it does
identify which of the three is absent, and `verdict` (`conformance/run:24-27`) prints the detail
through a quoted `printf`, so the `*` cannot re-glob. No change wanted.

title: CNF-18's GRANDCHILD-survived clause is unreachable for a defect that waits the call out: the fake's child sleeps 30s, the sleeping fake 60s
description:
Raised as a take-or-leave suggestion by the `opus` Reviewer of Run
`20260927T032120.020754216Z-2394293`'s Round 1 Panel, verified by the Manager and left out of that
Round's second brief as a change to the fake rather than to the diff under review.

`CNF-18`'s arms assert that the sleeping fake's SIGTERM-ignoring child does not survive. The child
sleeps 30 seconds (`conformance/fakes/agent:133`) while the fake it belongs to sleeps 60
(`RLOOP_FAKE_SLEEP_IMPLEMENTER=60`, `RLOOP_FAKE_SLEEP_PROBE=60`, `conformance/run:599`, `:631`), so
any defect that leaves rloop waiting the call out reaches that assertion after the child has exited
on its own. Measured in that Round: against a scratch copy of rloop-bash `02c6206` whose `spawn`
never registers the probe's group with the interrupt handler, `CNF-18`'s whole red is
`[probe: probe-0's fake got no SIGTERM]` — the `GRANDCHILD` clause stays green although the group
was never signalled.

The clause is not decoration: it still bites the defect where rloop exits without waiting, which is
`AGT-15`'s `rloop MUST NOT exit while any agent process it started, or the **Probe** (AGT-18), is
running`. What it cannot do today is redden on its own for a group that is merely never signalled.

## What to investigate

Whether the child's 30 seconds should outlast the fake's sleep — a child that is still alive when
the assertion runs is what makes the clause independently measurable — and what that costs every
other item whose fakes spawn one (`CNF-17`, `CNF-34`, and both `CNF-18` Implementer arms), since a
longer-lived child is a longer `kill_recorded` tail and a slower suite when an Implementation is
non-conformant. Per `AGENTS.md`, measure it: the change is worth making only if a mutant reddens
the `GRANDCHILD` clause alone, with every other verdict line unmoved.

Not this bead: the arm itself, which landed in that Round.
close_reason:

title: CNF-18 Probe-note suggestions from the Round 2 Panel: the DIR-4 quotation sits at advisory tier, and the 'so' arrives before its reason
description:
Three take-or-leave suggestions from the `opus` Reviewer of Run
`20260927T032120.020754216Z-2394293`'s Round 2 Panel, which found no defects. The Manager verified
each reading and declined all three as larger than that Round's brief asked for; the note they are
about is `CNF-18`'s, `06-conformance.md:209-226`, as `44bcefa` left it.

## The `DIR-4` quotation is advisory-tier where one apostrophe makes it blocking

The note reads `What `DIR-4` says of the probe's captures is `from the availability probe's stdout
and stderr`, `before the pick``. The Reviewer measured a corrupted copy of that quotation:
`ADVISORY CITATION: 06-conformance.md:220 attributes to DIR-4 (04-run-directory.md) words absent
from its body`, with `tools/check-all.sh` still exit 0 — so a later edit that breaks it is caught by
a human reading the gate's output and by nothing else. The `RUN-21` and `RUN-17` quotations in the
same note block instead of advising.

`tools/spec_text.py:185-186` is why: a possessive (`'s`) or a colon immediately before the quotation
makes the attribution `BLOCKING`, while a recognized introducer with prose between it and the
quotation stays `ADVISORY`. Written as ``DIR-4`'s `from the availability probe's stdout and
stderr`, `before the pick``, the same words block. Unmeasured by the Manager: whether that rewrite
keeps the sentence readable, since the quotation is the object of `says of the probe's captures`
and a possessive drops that clause.

## The `so` arrives before its reason

`06-conformance.md:217-219`: `that probe is the Run's first call, and `RUN-21` has it `after the Run
Directory exists`, `RUN-4` owning the creation, so the directory itself is all the suite can
portably read at that instant`. Those premises establish that the directory exists, not that nothing
else portably does; the support for the `so` is the sentence after it. Swapping the two sentences,
or making the second the `so` clause, removes the stumble.

## No pointer at `DIR-4`'s refusal clause

`04-run-directory.md:63-65` — `A Run refused at the pick (`RUN-22`) MUST leave the Run Directory
holding `probe-pick.out`, `probe-pick.err` and `probe-pick.md` and nothing else` — is the clause
that makes the note's reading concrete: the captures are expected present once the probe has
returned, which is the boundary the arm's SIGINT sits inside. The Reviewer judged a pointer there
worth more than the `F17` pointer Round 2 dropped.

## Not this bead

The arm itself, its assertions, call site, knobs and fake, all accepted in `d1bf313` and unchanged
by `44bcefa`; a Probe copy of `CNF-18`'s second-SIGINT clause; and the fake's child lifetime, which
is `rl-qxy`.

its tier: they are advisory unless they have their own blocking form.`

title: CNF-18's note opens a sentence with 'That probe' one clause after 'the Round's probe is never reached'
description:
`06-conformance.md:216-217`, the `CNF-18` note as `8b8d911` left it:

```
`once before the pick`, which the fake's one probe-sleep knob already lands on, so the Round's probe
is never reached and the Run costs no new knob. That probe is the Run's first call, and `RUN-21`
```

`That probe` means `RUN-21`'s `once before the pick` call, named at `:215-216`. The nearest preceding
noun phrase is `the Round's probe`, which the same clause says `is never reached` — bound there, `That
probe is the Run's first call` is false. The specification keeps the two calls apart by name: `DIR-4`
gives them separate rows (`04-run-directory.md:46-49`, `probe-pick.*` `before the pick` against
`probe-<r>.*` `Round `r`, before the Panel``), `06-conformance.md` writes `the probe before the pick`
in full at `:173`, `:322`, `:343`, `:398` and `:402` exactly where the distinction is needed, and
`:173-174` sets the two against each other in one sentence.

Raised by the `opus` Reviewer of Run `20260927T053937.832613661Z-2394293`'s Round 2 Panel, which
found nothing else, and verified by the Manager against three revisions before being declined as
larger than that Round's brief.

## Why it was not fixed in that Run

The competing binding is inherited, not introduced. At `c3a7060` and at `fef6dfa` the same sentence
read `… so the Round's probe is never reached and the Run costs no new knob. Its Run-Directory clause
is the weaker one deliberately: that probe is the Run's first call …`, and nothing between the two
phrases mentions a probe, so `the Round's probe` was already the nearest binding. What `8b8d911`
changed is the demonstrative's position: seating the colon moved `that probe` from mid-sentence to
sentence-initial `That probe`, abutting the competing noun. The wrong reading is also self-refuting
one clause later (`never reached` against `the Run's first call`), unlike the inverted reading
`8b8d911` was written to remove, which was coherent.

## What to do

Name the call instead of pointing at it, in the document's own words: `That probe` → `The probe before
the pick`, the phrase already used at the five sites above. It applies to the passage's one remaining
demonstrative the same remedy `8b8d911` applied to `that instant`, costs a rewrap of `:217-218`, and
touches no quotation — so the blocking form at `:219`, measured in that Run, cannot move. Measure the
gate anyway: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` and the corruption check on a scratch
copy.

Not this bead: `at the instant that probe is interrupted` at `:223`. Every probe in the intervening
`DIR-4` sentence is that same call, so it has no competing binding, and the Reviewer that raised this
said so.
